title: Did the Model Use That? Counterfactual Training Boosts Self-Attribution in Language Models
abstract: arXiv:2610.35295v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: A fundamental challenge for explainable and accountable language models is revealing how external information influences their answers. This paper examines whether models are self-attributive: that is, whether they indicate when -- and only when -- their responses to questions are influenced by information provided alongside the question. Furthermore, we explore how self-attribution can be improved through counterfactual training, which explicitly teaches models to distinguish between answers that do and do not depend on supplied information.   We found that most of the eleven frontier models rarely attribute influential information in their answers, and the rest attribute non-influential information. Training acknowledgment into reasoning does not fix this: the acknowledgment does not reach the final answer. translated_title: 模型用到了那条信息吗？反事实训练提升语言模型的自我归因能力
translated_abstract: 对于可解释、可问责的语言模型而言，一个根本性的挑战是揭示外部信息如何影响其回答。本文研究了模型是否具备“自我归因”能力：即模型是否能够在且仅在其对问题的回答受到随问题一同提供的信息影响时，明确指出这种影响。此外，我们探索了如何通过反事实训练来改进自我归因能力，该训练明确地教导模型区分哪些答案依赖所提供的信息、哪些不依赖。我们发现，在十一个前沿模型中，大多数模型很少在回答中归因那些实际产生影响的信息，而其余模型则归因了并未产生影响的信息。将“致谢声明”训练纳入推理过程也无法解决这一问题：因为致谢并不会传递到最终答案中。我们提出了CREDIT方法，利用反事实标签直接监督最终答案的自我归因，而无需……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 提出CREDIT方法，通过反事实训练直接监督模型最终答案的自我归因，使语言模型能够准确识别并声明其回答是否受到了所提供信息的影响。
en_tdlr: The paper introduces CREDIT, a counterfactual training approach that directly supervises final-answer self-attribution, enabling language models to accurately indicate whether—and only whether—their answers were influenced by information provided alongside the question.
